__meta.note: Base catalogue. Every other locale is scored against this one; see www/js/i18n.js.

__translatorNotes.literal: Keys listed in a locale's "__literal" array are expected to stay identical to English. File extensions (.srwb, .ipynb, .py) and kernel names (Python, Bash, Prolog, Lua, R) are identifiers, not prose — translating them would break what users type and search for.
__translatorNotes.rtl: In right-to-left locales, Latin identifiers keep their own direction inside the sentence. Write the sentence naturally in your language and leave the identifier as-is; the browser handles the bidirectional run.
__translatorNotes.placeholders: {name} placeholders are substituted at runtime. Keep them exactly as written; they may be reordered to suit your language's word order.

__senses.Cell-Notebook: The unit of code and its output in a notebook document. Not biological, not a spreadsheet cell, not a prison cell.
__senses.Run-Execute: To execute code. Not 'run' as in move quickly, and not a run/series of things.
__senses.Kernel-Interpreter: The language runtime that executes a cell. Not an operating-system kernel and not a seed.
__senses.Notebook-Document: A computational notebook document, in the Jupyter sense. Not a paper notebook and not a laptop.
__senses.Workbook-Bundle: A saved SciREPL bundle of notebooks and their packages. Distinct from Notebook-Document.
__senses.Package-Library: An installable software library. Not a parcel or a wrapper.
__senses.Language-Interface: The display language of the app's own menus and messages — the locale.
__senses.Language-Programming: The programming language a cell's code is written in (Python, Prolog, R…).
__senses.Scale-Size: Physical on-screen size. Not a musical scale, a weighing scale, or a map ratio.
__senses.Margin-Layout: Empty space at the edge of the interface. A layout term, not a printing margin or a profit margin.
__senses.Theme-Colours: A named set of interface colours. Not a topic or motif.
__senses.Reset-RestoreDefaults: Restore the default values. Not 'restart the device' and not 'erase data'.
__senses.Apply-Commit: Commit the pending changes in this dialog. Not 'apply for' something.
__senses.Import-LoadFile: Read a file into the app. Not importing goods.
__senses.Export-SaveFile: Write the user's work out to a file. Not exporting goods.
__senses.Session-AppState: The current working state of the app. Not a meeting or a class.

__context.appearance.themeAuto: Follow the operating system's light/dark setting.
__context.appearance.customise: Opens an editor. Trailing ellipsis means 'this opens a dialog' — keep it.
__context.appearance.buttonPreview: A live sample shown next to the control, not a preview of a document.
__context.appearance.advancedCss: CSS is a technical identifier and stays as-is.
__context.appearance.languageDetect: Detect the user's language from their device settings.
__context.appearance.languagePartial: Shown in a dropdown: the language name, then how much of the UI is translated.
__context.tour.editCellLanguage.body: 'All→' is a button label on screen; keep the arrow. 'cell' is a notebook cell.
__context.menu.showTour: Replays the first-run introduction. 'Tour' as in a guided walkthrough of the interface.
__context.appearance.showDrafts: A translation that exists but has not been checked by a native speaker. 'Under review' as in awaiting proofreading.
__context.appearance.languageDraft: Shown in the language dropdown next to an unreviewed translation.
__context.appearance.cssQuarantined: Shown when custom CSS made the menu unreachable and was rolled back. Reassuring, not accusatory — the CSS is kept, not deleted.
__context.appearance.cssRolledBack: Shown in the Advanced CSS editor when the entered CSS was rolled back for making the menu unreachable.

strings.menu.title: Menu
strings.appearance.title: Appearance
strings.appearance.topMarginHelp: Space above the header, so the app does not sit under the device status bar. Auto follows the device's reported safe area. Set 0 to remove it entirely.
strings.appearance.buttonScaleHelp: Scales the header buttons. Larger buttons are easier to hit on a touchscreen.
strings.appearance.themeEditorHelp: A theme is a set of colour variables. Edit the values below, then apply. Unknown names and non-colour values are rejected.
strings.appearance.advancedCssHelp: Raw CSS, applied last. This can make the app unusable — use Reset to defaults to recover.
strings.appearance.languageHelp: Only languages with a usable translation are listed. File extensions and kernel names stay in their original form in every language.
strings.tour.language.title: Choose your display language
strings.tour.language.body: This is the language of SciREPL's own menus and messages. It is separate from the programming language your code is written in.
strings.tour.menu.title: The menu
strings.tour.menu.body: Notebooks, import and export, packages, settings and appearance all live here.
strings.tour.help.title: Help
strings.tour.help.body: Documentation, the privacy policy, and this tour if you want to see it again.
strings.tour.newCellLanguage.title: Programming language for new cells
strings.tour.newCellLanguage.body: Pick the language your next cell will run in. Python, Prolog, Bash, JavaScript, R, Lua, TypR and ClojureScript are available.
strings.tour.editCell.title: Editing a cell
strings.tour.editCell.body: The pencil on any cell reopens it for editing and re-running. It appears once you have run something.
strings.tour.editCellLanguage.title: Changing a cell's programming language
strings.tour.editCellLanguage.body: While editing, this selector changes that one cell's language. "All→" applies your choice to every code cell in the notebook.
strings.help.installPurePythonPackagesFrom: Install pure-Python packages from PyPI with %pip install:
strings.help.noteOnlyPurePythonPackages: Note: Only pure-Python packages are supported. Packages with C extensions (e.g. psutil) require pre-compiled WASM wheels.
strings.help.noteOnlyRPackagesCompiled: Note: Only R packages compiled to WebAssembly are available. See repo.r-wasm.org for the package list.
strings.help.switchRUsingLanguageSelector: Switch to R using the language selector. The webR runtime (~50 MB) downloads on first use and is cached.
strings.help.switchPrologUsingLanguageSelector: Switch to Prolog using the language selector (Py → PL).
strings.help.scireplHasSharedvfsSharedVirtual: SciREPL has a SharedVFS (shared virtual filesystem) that lets all kernels read and write to the same files. Files under /shared/ and /tmp/ are accessible from every language.
strings.help.pythonUseStandardOpenShared: Python — Use standard open() with /shared/ paths. Files are synced to SharedVFS automatically after each cell execution.
strings.help.rUseSharedfsWriteSharedfs: R — Use sharedfs_write() and sharedfs_read() helpers to access shared files.
strings.help.bashBrushWasmShellHas: Bash — The brush-wasm shell has a built-in bridge to SharedVFS.
strings.help.packagesBundlesAmpWorkbooksWhen: Packages, bundles & workbooks: When you install an item from Browse Packages, Bundles & Workbooks, bundle dependencies are installed first and files with /shared/ destination paths are written to SharedVFS automatically. Package files targeting a specific kernel (e.g., Prolog modules at /user/) go to that kernel's own filesystem.
strings.help.browsingFilesOpenMenuFiles: Browsing files: Open Menu → Files & Storage to browse. Select SharedVFS from the dropdown to see shared files, or select a kernel (Python, Prolog) to see its internal filesystem. Use the Show empty folders checkbox to toggle visibility of empty directories.
strings.help.uploadingUseUploadFileButton: Uploading: Use the "Upload File" button at the top of Files & Storage to upload files directly into SharedVFS. Set the destination path (default: /shared/data/) before uploading.
strings.help.exportDocumentChooseDocumentFormat: Export Document — Choose a document format and image handling:
strings.help.htmlSelfContainedFileDark: HTML — Self-contained file with dark theme, code, and output. Choose "Separate files" for a .html.zip with an images/ folder.
strings.help.markdownFencedCodeBlocksLatex: Markdown — Fenced code blocks, LaTeX math, and markdown tables. "Separate files" uses GitHub-compatible ![alt](images/X.png) references in a .md.zip.
strings.help.pdfOpensBrowserPrintDialog: PDF — Opens the browser print dialog. Choose "Save as PDF" for a light-themed document.
strings.help.docxWordDocumentCodeBlocks: DOCX — Word document with code blocks, tables, images, and native Word equations (LaTeX math converted to editable OOXML formulas). Requires internet (library loaded on demand from CDN).
strings.help.latexTexFileAcademicPapers: LaTeX — .tex file for academic papers. Uses listings, amsmath, booktabs, graphicx. Exports as .tex.zip if images are present.
strings.help.exportWorkbooksAmpPackagesExport: Export Workbooks & Packages — Export notebooks and data:
strings.help.srwbScireplWorkbookNativeFormat: .srwb (SciREPL Workbook) — Native format for saving and restoring your workspace. Can hold multiple tabs in one file (like Excel sheets). Preserves per-cell language, cell IDs, and all SciREPL-specific state. Use this to back up your work or move it between devices. Not readable by Jupyter or other tools.
strings.help.ipynbJupyterNotebookUniversalNotebo: .ipynb (Jupyter Notebook) — Universal notebook format. One file per tab. Multi-language cells use %%magic commands (e.g. %%r, %%bash). Viewable in Jupyter, Colab, VS Code, and GitHub. Use this to share notebooks with others.
strings.help.packageArchiveZipTarTar: Package — Archive (.zip/.tar/.tar.gz) containing notebooks and data files from SharedVFS. Use this to share an entire project with its datasets.
strings.help.syntaxHighlightingCodeCellsDisplay: Syntax highlighting: Code cells display with syntax highlighting for Python, JavaScript, R, Bash, Prolog, and Lua. Exports (HTML, DOCX) also include highlighted code.
strings.help.ipynbImportOutputsWhenImporting: .ipynb import with outputs: When importing a .ipynb file that already contains outputs, they are displayed directly without re-executing the code. This allows fast viewing of notebooks from Jupyter, Colab, or previous SciREPL exports.
strings.help.switchLuaUsingLanguageSelector: Switch to Lua using the language selector. The Fengari runtime (~200 KB) downloads on first use from CDN.
strings.help.everyCellAccessibleAsVirtual: Every cell is accessible as a virtual file at /nb/. You can read and write cell code, output, language, and name from any kernel. Cells can be addressed three ways:
strings.help.tipGiveCellsNameClick: Tip: Give cells a name (click the cell label) so other cells can address them by name instead of fragile index numbers.
strings.help.eachCellRemembersItsLanguage: Each cell remembers its language. To change a cell's language, click ✎ to edit, then use the language dropdown. Click All→ to apply the language to all code cells in the notebook.
strings.help.putSourceOnFirstLine: Put #!source on the first line of a named TypR or Lua cell to keep highlighted code available through the Notebook VFS without executing it. The remaining directives are TypR-specific:
strings.help.sourceCellShowsSourceOnly: #!source — the cell shows Source only, intentionally has no Out [n], and remains readable through the Notebook VFS.
strings.help.typecheckTypeCheckFollowingCode: #!typecheck — type-check the following code without executing it.
strings.help.showRToggleGeneratedR: #!show-r — toggle generated R display for subsequent TypR executions.
strings.help.openMenuLanguagesShowHide: Open Menu → Languages to show or hide languages in the cell dropdown. Unchecking a language removes it from the selector but doesn't unload its runtime. All languages are enabled by default. Your preferences are saved across sessions.
strings.renameCell.enterNameCellEmptyClear: Enter a name for this cell (empty to clear):
strings.languages.enableDisableLanguagesCellDrop: Enable or disable languages in the cell dropdown.
strings.packageCatalog.oneClickInstallPackagesDe: One-click install packages, dependency-aware workbook bundles, and individual workbook templates into SciREPL.
strings.prologSettings.uploadAnyFileSharedFilesy: Upload any file to the shared filesystem, accessible from all kernels.
strings.prologSettings.browsePersistentStorageKe: Browse persistent storage and kernel-specific filesystems.
strings.vfsFilePreview.downloadFileFromUrlInto: Download a file from a URL into the virtual filesystem.
strings.privacy.scireplDesignedBePrivacyRespecti: SciREPL is designed to be a privacy-respecting application. All code execution happens locally on your device. We do not collect, store, or transmit any personal data to our servers.
strings.privacy.scireplStoresFollowingDataLocall: SciREPL stores the following data locally on your device using localStorage:
strings.privacy.yourSessionHistoryCodeCells: Your session history (code cells and their types)
strings.privacy.dataNeverLeavesYourDevice: This data never leaves your device. You can clear it at any time via Menu > Clear History.
strings.privacy.scireplBundlesMostItsRendering: SciREPL bundles most of its rendering libraries (Plotly.js, KaTeX, marked.js) directly in the app to minimize network requests. However, the following resources are loaded from third-party CDNs:
strings.privacy.pyodidePythonRuntime25mbFrom: Pyodide (Python runtime, ~25MB) — from cdn.jsdelivr.net. Loaded on first launch and cached locally for subsequent use.
strings.privacy.swiPrologWasmPrologRuntime: SWI-Prolog WASM (Prolog runtime, ~10MB) — from SWI-Prolog.github.io. Loaded only when Prolog is first used, and cached locally.
strings.privacy.koFiWidgetSupportButton: Ko-fi widget (support button in Help screen) — from storage.ko-fi.com
strings.privacy.whenTheseResourcesFetchedCdn: When these resources are fetched, the CDN providers may receive:
strings.privacy.yourDeviceSUserAgent: Your device's user agent string (browser/OS information)
strings.privacy.cachingUsedMinimizeConnectionsCd: Caching is used to minimize connections to CDN networks — after the initial download, Pyodide and its packages are served from the local cache.
strings.privacy.yourPythonCodeSessionData: Your Python code, session data, and exported files are never transmitted to any server.
strings.privacy.scireplProvidesFileFetchingFeatu: SciREPL provides a file-fetching feature that allows notebook code to download files from URLs you specify. When you use this feature (e.g., fetch_file in Prolog, or via the Prolog Settings panel), the request is made directly from your device to the specified URL. The remote server will receive your IP address and standard HTTP headers. SciREPL does not proxy, log, or monitor these requests.
strings.privacy.allPythonCodeYouEnter: All Python code you enter is executed locally on your device using Pyodide (Python compiled to WebAssembly). No code is sent to any remote server for execution.
strings.privacy.whenYouExportNotebookIpynb: When you export a notebook (.ipynb), the file is created locally on your device. If you choose to share it (via the system share sheet), the destination is determined by your choice. SciREPL does not control or monitor where you share exported files.
strings.privacy.scireplDoesNotIncludeAny: SciREPL does not include any analytics, crash reporting, advertising SDKs, or tracking mechanisms.
strings.privacy.scireplDoesNotKnowinglyCollect: SciREPL does not knowingly collect any information from children. The app does not require account creation or collect personal information of any kind.
strings.privacy.ifAdditionalLanguageRuntimesAdde: If additional language runtimes are added (e.g. Prolog, R), they may also be loaded from CDNs and cached locally, subject to the same metadata exposure described above. This policy will be updated to reflect any changes.
strings.privacy.youUseScireplEntirelyAt: You use SciREPL entirely at your own risk. Code execution occurs locally on your device and the developers are not responsible for any consequences of code you choose to run.
strings.runtimeDownload.runtimeRequiresDownloadI: This runtime requires a download. It will be cached by the browser for future use.
strings.export.letBrowserDecideStripsBackgrounds: Let browser decide (strips backgrounds on print)
strings.export.oneFilePerTabMagic: One file per tab, %%magic for multi-language
strings.export.allowCellsModifyOtherCells: Allow cells to modify other cells
strings.help.runtimeVersions: Runtime versions: Languages loaded from CDN (R, Prolog) have a version field on the Languages page. Leave it blank to use the pinned default (recommended), enter a tag like v0.5.4 to use a specific version, or enter latest for the rolling release. The rolling release can occasionally serve mismatched files (e.g. ASM_CONSTS[code] is not a function) — if that happens, switch to the pinned default and clear the SciREPL cache.
strings.help.includesFeatureList: Includes: Multi-language (Python, R, Prolog, Bash, JavaScript, Lua), editable cells, markdown cells, session persistence with auto-save and crash recovery, Math Mode palette, .ipynb import/export with output preservation, .srwb workbook format, rich export (HTML, Markdown, PDF, DOCX with native equations, LaTeX) with syntax highlighting, virtual filesystem, search paths, URL file fetching, multi-notebook support, package catalog with one-click install, language settings, package format (.zip/.tar.gz)
strings.appearance.showDraftsHelp: Most translations have not yet been checked by a speaker of the language. They are offered anyway, and labelled, because an interface you can read beats one you cannot. Turn this off to see only reviewed translations.
strings.appearance.cssQuarantined: Your custom CSS hid the menu button, so it has been turned off. It is kept in Appearance → Advanced so you can edit it.
strings.appearance.cssRolledBack: This CSS was turned off because it hid the menu. Edit it and apply again.
